## `#[doc(auto_cfg(hide(a, values(::b))))]` is accepted without a word: a non-identifier path in `auto_cfg` is skipped, not reported

crates/blaze-diagnostics/src/lints/syntax/attrs/doc.rs: in `auto_cfg`, `MetaArgs::None` with a non-word path (~538: `continue 'main`) and `values` named by a non-word (~544). In `auto_cfg_values`, `Item::Meta(sub)` with a non-word path (~599: `let Some(ident) = sub.path.word() else { continue };`). Each is commented "Not an identifier: an error." but emits nothing, so a malformed attribute builds. rustc (`rustc_attr_parsing` doc `parse_auto_cfg`/`parse_auto_cfg_values`, `cx.expected_identifier`): E0565 "malformed `doc` attribute input" at the attribute, labelled "expected a valid identifier here" at the path (`::b`). Fix: emit that error at each of the three places (one per attribute, as rustc stops at the first). Test: blaze-diagnostics tests::items::attrs::doc::auto_cfg_values_are_identifiers (empty output in rounds 12-15; it now asserts one error at line 5 naming `doc`).
